By induction,

\[
P_n(x)=x^{5n}-x^{5(n-1)}+\cdots+(-1)^n
=\sum_{k=0}^n (-1)^{n-k}x^{5k}.
\]

Let \(y=x^5\). Since \(x\mapsto x^5\) is a bijection on \(\mathbb R\), real roots of \(P_n(x)\) correspond to real roots in \(y\).

For \(y\neq -1\),

\[
P_n(x)=(-1)^n\sum_{k=0}^n (-y)^k
=(-1)^n\frac{1-(-y)^{n+1}}{1+y}
=\frac{y^{n+1}+(-1)^n}{y+1}.
\]

Also, at \(y=-1\) (i.e. \(x=-1\)),

\[
P_n(-1)=(-1)^n(n+1)\neq 0,
\]

so \(x=-1\) is never a root.

Thus any real root must satisfy

\[
y^{n+1}+(-1)^n=0,\qquad y\neq -1.
\]

- If \(n\) is even, then \(n+1\) is odd, so \(y^{n+1}=-1\) gives \(y=-1\), which is excluded. Hence no real roots.
- If \(n\) is odd, then \(n+1\) is even, so \(y^{n+1}=1\) gives \(y=\pm1\). The value \(y=-1\) is excluded, while \(y=1\) gives \(x^5=1\), so \(x=1\).

Therefore,

\[
\boxed{
\begin{cases}
P_n(x)\text{ has no real roots}, & n\text{ even (including }n=0),\\[2mm]
P_n(x)\text{ has the unique real root }x=1, & n\text{ odd}.
\end{cases}
}
\]

27B·v4.method: Derive explicit sum formula, substitute y=x^5, use geometric sum to reduce to y^{n+1}+(-1)^n=0, split by parity of n.
